metadata.title: Are Transformers universal approximators of sequence-to-sequence functions?
metadata.authors: Chulhee Yun, Srinadh Bhojanapalli, Ankit Singh Rawat, Sashank J. Reddi, Sanjiv Kumar

nodes.name: Transformer block
nodes.statement: A Transformer block $t^{h,m,r}: \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \to \mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ is the composition $\mathrm{ff}(\mathrm{attn}(\mathbf{X}))$, where $\mathrm{attn}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathbf{X} + \sum_{i=1}^h \mathbf{W}_O^i \mathbf{W}_V^i \mathbf{X}\, \mathrm{sfmx}[(\mathbf{W}_K^i \mathbf{X})^T \mathbf{W}_Q^i \mathbf{X}]$ and $\mathrm{ff}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathrm{attn}(\mathbf{X}) + \mathbf{W}_2 \, \mathrm{ReLU}(\mathbf{W}_1 \mathrm{attn}(\mathbf{X}) + \mathbf{b}_1 \mathbf{1}_n^T) + \mathbf{b}_2 \mathbf{1}_n^T$.
nodes.statement_clean: A Transformer block consists of a multi-head self-attention layer with $h$ heads of head size $m$, followed by a token-wise two-layer feed-forward network with $r$ hidden units; both layers carry skip connections.

nodes.name: Transformer network class $\mathcal{T}^{h,m,r}$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{T}^{h,m,r} \defeq \{ g: \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \to \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \mid g \text{ is a composition of Transformer blocks } t^{h,m,r} \}$.

nodes.name: Permutation equivariant function
nodes.statement: $f: \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \to \mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ is permutation equivariant if $f(\mathbf{X} \mathbf{P}) = f(\mathbf{X}) \mathbf{P}$ for every permutation matrix $\mathbf{P}$.

nodes.name: Transformer with positional encoding $\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{P}}^{h,m,r}$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{P}}^{h,m,r} \defeq \{ g_{\mathrm{P}}(\mathbf{X}) = g(\mathbf{X} + \mathbf{E}) \mid g \in \mathcal{T}^{h,m,r}, \mathbf{E} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \}$, allowing trainable positional encodings $\mathbf{E}$.

nodes.name: Function distance $\mathrm{d}_p$
nodes.statement: For $f_1, f_2 : \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \to \mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ and $1 \leq p < \infty$, define $\mathrm{d}_p(f_1, f_2) \defeq (\int \|f_1(\mathbf{X}) - f_2(\mathbf{X})\|_p^p \, d\mathbf{X})^{1/p}$.

nodes.name: Target class $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PE}}$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PE}}$ is the set of all continuous permutation equivariant functions with compact support mapping $\mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ to $\mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$.

nodes.name: Target class $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{CD}}$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{CD}}$ is the set of all continuous functions mapping a compact domain in $\mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ to $\mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ (no permutation equivariance restriction).

nodes.name: Contextual mapping
nodes.section: 3.1 A key step: self-attention layers can implement contextual mappings
nodes.statement: Given finite $\mathfrak{L} \subset \mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$, a map $q: \mathfrak{L} \to \mathbb{R}^{1 \times n}$ is a contextual mapping if (i) for any $\mathbf{L} \in \mathfrak{L}$ the $n$ entries of $q(\mathbf{L})$ are all distinct, and (ii) for any $\mathbf{L} \neq \mathbf{L}' \in \mathfrak{L}$, all entries of $q(\mathbf{L})$ and $q(\mathbf{L}')$ are distinct.

nodes.name: Piece-wise constant class $\overline{\mathcal{F}}_{\mathrm{PE}}(\delta)$
nodes.section: 3.2 Proof of the universal approximation theorem
nodes.statement: $\overline{\mathcal{F}}_{\mathrm{PE}}(\delta) \defeq \{ f: \mathbf{X} \mapsto \sum_{\mathbf{L} \in \mathbb{G}_\delta} \mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{L}} \mathbf{1}\{\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{S}_{\mathbf{L}}\} \mid f \text{ permutation equivariant}, \mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{L}} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \}$ on the grid $\mathbb{G}_\delta = \{0, \delta, \dots, 1-\delta\}^{d \times n}$ with cubes $\mathbb{S}_{\mathbf{L}}$ of width $\delta$.

nodes.name: Modified Transformer class $\overline{\mathcal{T}}^{h,m,r}$
nodes.section: 3.2 Proof of the universal approximation theorem
nodes.statement: $\overline{\mathcal{T}}^{h,m,r}$ is the function class of Transformer networks where $\mathrm{sfmx}[\cdot]$ is replaced by the hardmax $\mathrm{hdmx}[\cdot]$ and the ReLU is replaced by an activation $\phi \in \Phi$, the set of piece-wise linear functions with at most three pieces, at least one of them constant.

nodes.name: Subset $\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$
nodes.statement: $\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta \defeq \{ \mathbf{L} \in \mathbb{G}_\delta \mid \mathbf{L}_{:,i} \neq \mathbf{L}_{:,j} \text{ for all } i \neq j\}$, the subset of grid points whose columns are all distinct.

nodes.name: Extended grid $\mathbb{G}_\delta^+$
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{G}_\delta^+ \defeq \{-\delta^{-nd}, 0, \delta, \dots, 1-\delta\}^{d \times n}$, the extended grid that includes a sentinel value $-\delta^{-nd}$ for entries outside $[0,1]$.

nodes.name: Permutation equivariance of Transformer blocks
nodes.statement: A Transformer block $t^{h,m,r}$ defines a permutation equivariant map from $\mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ to $\mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$.
assumptions: $t^{h,m,r}$ is a Transformer block as in $\mathrm{Definition}\ \mathrm{DP16.1}$

nodes.name: Universal approximation (permutation equivariant)
nodes.statement: Let $1 \leq p < \infty$ and $\epsilon > 0$. For any $f \in \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PE}}$, there exists a Transformer network $g \in \mathcal{T}^{2,1,4}$ such that $\mathrm{d}_p(f, g) \leq \epsilon$.
conclusions: Constants $h=2, m=1, r=4$ do not depend on $n$ or $d$

nodes.name: Universal approximation with positional encoding
nodes.statement: Let $1 \leq p < \infty$ and $\epsilon > 0$. For any $f \in \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{CD}}$, there exists a Transformer network $g \in \mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{P}}^{2,1,4}$ such that $\mathrm{d}_p(f, g) \leq \epsilon$.
conclusions: $\exists\, g \in \mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{P}}^{2,1,4}$ with trainable positional encoding $\mathbf{E}$ such that $\mathrm{d}_p(f,g) \leq \epsilon$

nodes.name: Modified Transformers approximate piece-wise constants
nodes.section: 3.2 Proof of the universal approximation theorem (Proposition 1)
nodes.statement: For each $\overline f \in \overline{\mathcal{F}}_{\mathrm{PE}}(\delta)$ and $1 \leq p < \infty$, there exists $\overline g \in \overline{\mathcal{T}}^{2,1,1}$ such that $\mathrm{d}_p(\overline f, \overline g) = O(\delta^{d/p})$.

nodes.name: Piece-wise constant approximation of $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PE}}$
nodes.statement: For any $f \in \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PE}}$ and $1 \leq p < \infty$, there exists $\delta^* > 0$ and $\overline f \in \overline{\mathcal{F}}_{\mathrm{PE}}(\delta^*)$ with $\mathrm{d}_p(f, \overline f) \leq \epsilon/3$.

nodes.name: Approximating modified Transformers by original Transformers
nodes.statement: For each $\overline g \in \overline{\mathcal{T}}^{2,1,1}$ and $1 \leq p < \infty$, there exists $g \in \mathcal{T}^{2,1,4}$ with $\mathrm{d}_p(\overline g, g) \leq \epsilon/3$.
conclusions: Hardmax can be approximated by softmax via parameter rescaling; each $\phi \in \Phi$ can be approximated by a sum of four $\mathrm{ReLU}$s

nodes.name: Quantization by feed-forward layers
nodes.statement: There exists $g_{\mathrm{q}}: \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \to \mathbb{G}_\delta^+$ composed of $\frac{d}{\delta} + d$ token-wise feed-forward layers with $r=1$ and activations in $\Phi$ that applies the scalar quantization $g_{\mathrm{q}}^{\mathrm{ent}}$ entry-wise.
assumptions: Scalar quantizer $g_{\mathrm{q}}^{\mathrm{ent}}(t) = k\delta$ if $k\delta \leq t < (k+1)\delta$ and $-\delta^{-nd}$ otherwise
conclusions: A modified-Transformer feed-forward stack of $\tfrac{d}{\delta}+d$ layers realises $g_{\mathrm{q}}: \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \to \mathbb{G}_\delta^+$
$g_{\mathrm{q}}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathbf{L}$ for $\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{S}_{\mathbf{L}}$, and entries outside $[0,1]$ map to $-\delta^{-nd}$

nodes.name: Contextual mapping by self-attention layers
nodes.statement: Assume $n \geq 2$ and $\delta^{-1} \geq 2$. There exist $g_{\mathrm{c}}: \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \to \mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ composed of $\delta^{-d}+1$ self-attention layers ($h=2, m=1$) with $\mathrm{hdmx}$, a vector $\mathbf{u} \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and constants $0 < t_l < t_r$ such that $q(\mathbf{L}) = \mathbf{u}^T g_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathbf{L})$ has distinct entries for every $\mathbf{L} \in \widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$, distinct entries across non-permutation pairs $\mathbf{L},\mathbf{L}'$, lies in $[t_l, t_r]$ on $\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$, and lies outside $[t_l,t_r]$ on $\mathbb{G}_\delta^+ \setminus \widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$.
conclusions: $\exists\, g_{\mathrm{c}}$ composed of $\delta^{-d}+1$ self-attention layers ($h=2, m=1$) implementing a permutation equivariant contextual mapping on $\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$
Property 1: entries of $q(\mathbf{L})$ are all distinct
Property 2: entries across non-permutation pairs are all distinct

nodes.name: Function value mapping by feed-forward layers
nodes.section: 4.3 Function value mapping by feed-forward layers (Lemma 6)
nodes.statement: Let $g_{\mathrm{c}}$ be the function from Lemma~$\mathrm{LP16.4}$. Then there exists $g_{\mathrm{v}}: \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \to \mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ composed of $O(n(1/\delta)^{dn}/n!)$ token-wise feed-forward layers ($r=1$) with activations in $\Phi$ that maps each $g_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathbf{L})_{:,j}$ to $(\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{L}})_{:,j}$ on $\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$ and to $\mathbf{0}_d$ on $\mathbb{G}_\delta^+ \setminus \widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$.
conclusions: $\exists\, g_{\mathrm{v}}$ defined token-wise via $g_{\mathrm{v}}^{\mathrm{tkn}}: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$ with $g_{\mathrm{v}}^{\mathrm{tkn}}(g_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathbf{L})_{:,j}) = (\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{L}})_{:,j}$ on $\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$ and $= \mathbf{0}_d$ on the complement

nodes.name: Bounds and one-to-one property of $\widetilde l_n$
nodes.statement: After $n$ selective shift operations, $\widetilde l_n = \mathbf{u}^T \widetilde{\mathbf{L}}_{:,n}$ satisfies $\delta^{-(n-1)d+1}(\delta^{-d}-1) \leq \widetilde l_n \leq \delta^{-nd+1}(\delta^{-d}-1) - \delta(\delta^{-d}-1)^2$, and the map $[l_1, \dots, l_n] \mapsto \widetilde l_n$ (with $l_1 < \dots < l_n$) is one-to-one.

nodes.name: Selective shift operation
nodes.statement: An attention layer $\mathbf{Z} \mapsto \mathbf{Z} + \Psi(\mathbf{Z}; b_Q, b'_Q)$ built from two hardmax attention heads of size $1$ that shifts the first coordinate of any column with $\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z}_{:,j} \in (b_Q, b'_Q)$ by $\max_k \mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z}_{:,k} - \min_k \mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z}_{:,k}$, while leaving other columns untouched.
output: Updated matrix where coordinates with $\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z}_{:,j} \in (b_Q, b'_Q)$ have their first row shifted up by $\max_k \mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z}_{:,k} - \min_k \mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z}_{:,k}$
nodes.pseudocode: Define $\psi(\mathbf{Z}; b_Q) = \mathbf{e}^{(1)} \mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z}\, \mathrm{hdmx}[(\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z})^T(\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z} - b_Q \mathbf{1}_n^T)]$. Set $\Psi(\mathbf{Z}; b_Q, b'_Q) = \psi(\mathbf{Z}; b_Q) - \psi(\mathbf{Z}; b'_Q)$. Output $\mathbf{Z} + \Psi(\mathbf{Z}; b_Q, b'_Q)$.

nodes.name: Modified Transformer construction $\overline g = g_{\mathrm{v}} \circ g_{\mathrm{c}} \circ g_{\mathrm{q}}$
nodes.statement: Construct a modified Transformer network as $\overline g = g_{\mathrm{v}} \circ g_{\mathrm{c}} \circ g_{\mathrm{q}}$: feed-forward quantization, then self-attention contextual mapping, then feed-forward value mapping.
output: Modified Transformer $\overline g \in \overline{\mathcal{T}}^{2,1,1}$ with $\mathrm{d}_p(\overline f, \overline g) = O(\delta^{d/p})$

nodes.name: Bi-linear projection layer (BProj)
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{BProj}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathbf{X} + \mathbf{W}_O \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_P$, a residual layer that left- and right-multiplies the token embedding matrix.
nodes.origin_citation: Gong et al. 2013 (motivated by Ailon \& Chazelle 2009)

nodes.name: Depth-wise separable convolution layer (SepConv)
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{SepConv}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathbf{X} + \mathbf{W}_O (\mathbf{X} * \mathbf{W}_C)$, where each row of $\mathbf{X}$ is convolved with the corresponding row of $\mathbf{W}_C \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times k}$.
nodes.origin_citation: Sifre 2014; Chollet 2017; Kaiser et al. 2017; Wu et al. 2019

nodes.name: Universal approximation of sequence-to-sequence functions
nodes.statement: Given a target class of continuous sequence-to-sequence functions, can fixed-width Transformer networks (with $h, m, r$ independent of $n, d$) approximate every function in the class to arbitrary $\ell^p$ accuracy?

nodes.name: Sentence embedding example: 'I am happy' vs. 'I am Bob'
nodes.statement: Two sentences fed as $\mathbf{X} = [\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{I}}, \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{am}}, \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{happy}}]$ and $\widetilde{\mathbf{X}} = [\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{I}}, \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{am}}, \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Bob}}]$ illustrate why the model must map the two occurrences of 'I' to different output values, motivating the contextual-mapping requirement.

nodes.name: BERT-base hybrid Transformer/SepConv on SQuAD and MNLI
nodes.statement: Replacing the lower self-attention layers of $\mathrm{BERT}_{\mathrm{BASE}}$ (12 Transformer blocks) with depth-wise separable convolutions, and evaluating on SQuAD and MNLI; replacing $1$ or $2$ self-attention layers improves performance, while replacing more hurts it.

nodes.name: BProj / SepConv / Average Attention vs. Transformer on MNLI and Masked LM
nodes.statement: On masked-LM pre-training and MNLI, replacing self-attention with $\mathrm{BProj}$ ($72.3\%$), $\mathrm{SepConv}$ ($73\%$) or average attention ($66\%$) yields lower MNLI accuracy than the full Transformer ($78.2\%$); average attention is clearly worst, ruling out the trivial-task explanation.

nodes.name: Tightness of the construction
nodes.statement: Theorem $\mathrm{TP16.1}$ requires $O(n(1/\delta)^{dn}/n!)$ Transformer blocks of constant width and total $O(dn(1/\delta)^{dn}/n!)$ parameters; the exponential dependence is unavoidable in the worst case (memorization argument), and Transformers are more parameter-efficient than residual networks for permutation equivariant functions.

nodes.name: Universal approximation $\neq$ Turing completeness
nodes.statement: Turing completeness for Transformers (Perez et al. 2019, infinite precision) concerns computation on discrete formal languages; universal approximation concerns continuous functions on a continuum. Neither implies the other.

nodes.name: Negligible measure of $\mathbb{G}_\delta \setminus \widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$
nodes.statement: $|\mathbb{G}_\delta \setminus \widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta| = O(\delta^d |\mathbb{G}_\delta|)$, so for small $\delta$ the set of inputs whose columns are not all distinct constitutes a negligible fraction of the grid.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim $\mathrm{ClP16.1}$ (permutation equivariance)
nodes.statement: Direct algebraic verification: using $\mathbf{P}\mathbf{P}^T = \mathbf{I}$ and $\mathrm{ReLU}(\mathbf{X}\mathbf{P}) = \mathrm{ReLU}(\mathbf{X})\mathbf{P}$, both $\mathrm{attn}$ and $\mathrm{ff}$ are shown to commute with right-multiplication by a permutation matrix.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem $\mathrm{TP16.1}$ (universal approximation, perm. equivariant)
nodes.section: 3.2 Proof of the universal approximation theorem
nodes.statement: Three-step construction: (1) approximate $f$ by piece-wise constant $\overline f \in \overline{\mathcal{F}}_{\mathrm{PE}}(\delta)$ using uniform continuity (Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.1}$); (2) approximate $\overline f$ by modified Transformer $\overline g \in \overline{\mathcal{T}}^{2,1,1}$ (Proposition $\mathrm{PrP16.1}$); (3) approximate $\overline g$ by original Transformer $g \in \mathcal{T}^{2,1,4}$ (Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.2}$). Triangle inequality gives $\mathrm{d}_p(f,g) \leq 2\epsilon/3 + O(\delta^{d/p})$, choose $\delta$ small.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition $\mathrm{PrP16.1}$ (modified Transformer approximates piece-wise constants)
nodes.statement: Define $\overline g = g_{\mathrm{v}} \circ g_{\mathrm{c}} \circ g_{\mathrm{q}}$ from Lemmas $\mathrm{LP16.3}$, $\mathrm{LP16.4}$, $\mathrm{LP16.5}$. Show $\overline g(\mathbf{X}) = \overline f(\mathbf{X})$ on $\bigcup_{\mathbf{L} \in \widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta} \mathbb{S}_{\mathbf{L}}$ and $\overline g(\mathbf{X}) = \mathbf{0}$ elsewhere; the discrepancy set has measure $O(\delta^d)$, giving $\mathrm{d}_p(\overline f, \overline g) = O(\delta^{d/p})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.1}$ (piecewise-constant approximation)
nodes.statement: Use uniform continuity of $f$ on its compact support: pick $\delta$ such that $\|\mathbf{X}-\mathbf{Y}\|_\infty < \delta \implies \|f(\mathbf{X})-f(\mathbf{Y})\|_p < \epsilon/3$. Define $\overline f(\mathbf{X}) = \sum_{\mathbf{L}} f(\mathbf{C}_{\mathbf{L}}) \mathbf{1}\{\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{S}_{\mathbf{L}}\}$ where $\mathbf{C}_{\mathbf{L}}$ is the cube center; permutation equivariance is preserved.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.2}$ (softmax/ReLU approximation)
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{sfmx}[\lambda \mathbf{A}] \to \mathrm{hdmx}[\mathbf{A}]$ as $\lambda \to \infty$, so hardmax can be approximated by softmax via parameter rescaling. Each three-piece $\phi \in \Phi$ is approximated arbitrarily well by a sum of four ReLUs, so a hidden width of 4 suffices.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.3}$ (quantization)
nodes.statement: Construct $1/\delta + 1$ feed-forward layers per row. The first layer clips entries outside $[0,1]$ to $-\delta^{-nd}$; the remaining $1/\delta$ layers each quantize entries in $[k\delta, k\delta+\delta)$ to $k\delta$. Repeat row-wise for $d$ rows.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.4}$ (contextual mapping)
nodes.statement: Define the column-id vector $\mathbf{u}=(1,\delta^{-1},\dots,\delta^{-d+1})$ giving a bijection $\mathbf{L}_{:,j} \mapsto \mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{L}_{:,j}$. Stack $(1/\delta)^d$ selective-shift attention layers sweeping each $l \in [0:\delta:\delta^{-d+1}-\delta]$, then a final global-shift layer. Verify the four properties on three categories of input ($\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$, $\mathbb{G}_\delta \setminus \widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$, $\mathbb{G}_\delta^+ \setminus \mathbb{G}_\delta$).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.5}$ (value mapping)
nodes.statement: Use one ``bump'' feed-forward layer $\mathbf{Z} \mapsto \mathbf{Z} - (M+1)\mathbf{1}_n \phi(\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z})$ to zero-out outputs from $\mathbb{G}_\delta^+ \setminus \widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$, then $d$ layers to clip negatives to zero, then one feed-forward layer per unique value $\mathbf{u}^T g_{\mathrm{c}}(\overline{\mathbf{L}})_{:,j}$ that adds $((\mathbf{A}_{\overline{\mathbf{L}}})_{:,j} - g_{\mathrm{c}}(\overline{\mathbf{L}})_{:,j})$ exactly when $\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z}$ matches that value.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.6}$ (sublemma 1: bounds and one-to-one)
nodes.statement: Direct algebraic bounding from the recurrence $\widetilde l_n = l_n + \sum_{k=1}^{n-1} \delta^{-kd}(l_{n-k}-l_{n-k+1}) + \delta^{-nd}(l_n-l_1)$ gives the lower and upper bounds. One-to-one is shown by 'coarse-resolution' contradiction: $\delta^{-d}$ powers of distinct order cannot cancel each other modulo finer-resolution differences.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem $\mathrm{TP16.2}$ (universal approximation with positional encoding)
nodes.statement: Modify the proof of Theorem $\mathrm{TP16.1}$: choose positional encoding $\mathbf{E}$ with $\mathbf{E}_{:,j} = (j-1)\mathbf{1}_d$ so that $\mathbf{X}+\mathbf{E}$ has columns in disjoint cubes $[j-1, j]^d$. Re-run quantization on the enlarged grid, contextual mapping (which now reduces to Category 1 only), and value mapping ($O(n(1/\delta)^{dn})$ layers, no $1/n!$ saving since equivariance is removed).

nodes.name: Step 1: Approximate $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PE}}$ with piece-wise constant functions
nodes.statement: Use Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.1}$: pick $\overline f \in \overline{\mathcal{F}}_{\mathrm{PE}}(\delta)$ with $\mathrm{d}_p(f, \overline f) \leq \epsilon/3$.

nodes.name: Step 2: Approximate $\overline f$ by modified Transformer
nodes.statement: Use Proposition $\mathrm{PrP16.1}$: pick $\overline g \in \overline{\mathcal{T}}^{2,1,1}$ with $\mathrm{d}_p(\overline f, \overline g) = O(\delta^{d/p})$.

nodes.name: Step 3: Approximate $\overline g$ by original Transformer
nodes.statement: Use Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.2}$: pick $g \in \mathcal{T}^{2,1,4}$ with $\mathrm{d}_p(\overline g, g) \leq \epsilon/3$.

nodes.name: Combine via triangle inequality
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{d}_p(f,g) \leq \mathrm{d}_p(f,\overline f) + \mathrm{d}_p(\overline f,\overline g) + \mathrm{d}_p(\overline g, g) \leq 2\epsilon/3 + O(\delta^{d/p})$. Choosing $\delta$ small enough yields $\mathrm{d}_p(f,g) \leq \epsilon$.

nodes.name: Quantize input to grid
nodes.statement: Apply $g_{\mathrm{q}}$ from Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.3}$: $\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{S}_{\mathbf{L}}$ maps to $\mathbf{L} \in \mathbb{G}_\delta^+$.

nodes.name: Compute contextual mapping
nodes.statement: Apply $g_{\mathrm{c}}$ from Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.4}$: each $\mathbf{L} \in \widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$ is sent to a contextual embedding whose entries uniquely encode $\mathbf{L}$ up to permutation.

nodes.name: Map contextual values to $\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{L}}$
nodes.statement: Apply $g_{\mathrm{v}}$ from Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.5}$: token-wise feed-forward layers send $g_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathbf{L})_{:,j}$ to $(\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{L}})_{:,j}$ on $\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$ and to $\mathbf{0}$ otherwise.

nodes.name: Bound the error by measure of bad set
nodes.statement: $\overline g$ matches $\overline f$ on $\bigcup_{\mathbf{L} \in \widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta} \mathbb{S}_{\mathbf{L}}$ and outputs zero on the residual set of measure $O(\delta^d)$, giving $\mathrm{d}_p(\overline f, \overline g) \leq (B^p \delta^d)^{1/p} = O(\delta^{d/p})$.

nodes.name: Selective shift operation as the building block
nodes.statement: Show that two hardmax attention heads of size 1 implement $\Psi(\mathbf{Z}; b_Q, b'_Q)$, which selectively shifts entries with $\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z}_{:,j} \in (b_Q, b'_Q)$ by $\max - \min$, leaving others untouched.

nodes.name: Bijective column id $\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{L}_{:,j}$
nodes.statement: Choose $\mathbf{u} = (1,\delta^{-1},\dots,\delta^{-d+1})$. Then $\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{L}_{:,j}$ is a bijective 'column id' from $\{0,\delta,\dots,1-\delta\}^d$ onto $[0:\delta:\delta^{-d+1}-\delta]$, while sentinel columns map to negative values.

nodes.name: Stack $(1/\delta)^d$ shift layers + one global-shift layer
nodes.statement: Stack $(1/\delta)^d$ layers $\delta^{-d} \Psi(\cdot; l-\delta/2, l+\delta/2)$ for $l$ sweeping $[0:\delta:\delta^{-d+1}-\delta]$ in increasing order, then add one extra single-head layer $\delta^{-(n+1)d}\psi(\cdot;0)$.

nodes.name: Case 1: $\mathbf{L} \in \widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$
nodes.statement: All entries in $[0,1-\delta]$ and all columns distinct. Iterated shifts produce $\widetilde l_1 < \widetilde l_2 < \dots < \widetilde l_n$ via the recurrence $\widetilde l_j = l_j + \sum_{k=1}^{j-1}\delta^{-kd}(l_{j-k}-l_{j-k+1}) + \delta^{-jd}(l_n - l_1)$. Apply Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.6}$ to verify Properties 1 and 2.

nodes.name: Case 2: $\mathbf{L} \in \mathbb{G}_\delta \setminus \widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$
nodes.statement: Duplicate columns yield only $n' < n$ distinct values; the upper bound on $\widetilde l_n$ is strictly smaller than the Category-1 lower bound, so $\mathbf{u}^T g_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathbf{L})_{:,j} < t_l$, verifying Property 4.

nodes.name: Case 3: $\mathbf{L} \in \mathbb{G}_\delta^+ \setminus \mathbb{G}_\delta$
nodes.statement: Some entry equals $-\delta^{-nd}$, forcing some $l_j < 0$. Either all $l_j < 0$ (input unchanged, then global shift pushes further negative) or shifts push positive entries above $\delta^{-(2n+2)d+1} > t_r$. Property 4 holds.

nodes.name: Verify Properties 3 and 4 (interval $[t_l,t_r]$)
nodes.statement: Set $t_l = \delta^{-2nd+1}(\delta^{-d}-1)$ and $t_r = \delta^{-(2n+1)d+1}(\delta^{-d}-1)$. Combining the three cases verifies all four properties of Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.4}$.

nodes.name: Zero out outputs for $\mathbb{G}_\delta^+ \setminus \widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$
nodes.statement: Add a feed-forward layer $\mathbf{Z} \mapsto \mathbf{Z} - (M+1)\mathbf{1}_n \phi(\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z})$ with $\phi$ vanishing on $[t_l,t_r]$ and equal to 1 elsewhere; this leaves $g_{\mathrm{c}}(\widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta)$ unchanged and shifts the rest strictly negative.

nodes.name: Clip negatives to zero
nodes.statement: Add $d$ layers $\mathbf{Z} \mapsto \mathbf{Z} + \mathbf{e}^{(i)} \phi((\mathbf{e}^{(i)})^T \mathbf{Z})$ with $\phi(t) = -t$ for $t<0$ and $0$ otherwise, sending all strictly negative entries to zero.

nodes.name: Per-value bump layer maps $g_{\mathrm{c}}(\overline{\mathbf{L}})_{:,j} \mapsto (\mathbf{A}_{\overline{\mathbf{L}}})_{:,j}$
nodes.statement: For each $\overline{\mathbf{L}} \in \widetilde{\mathbb{G}}_\delta$ and each $j \in [n]$ add a layer $\mathbf{Z} \mapsto \mathbf{Z} + ((\mathbf{A}_{\overline{\mathbf{L}}})_{:,j} - g_{\mathrm{c}}(\overline{\mathbf{L}})_{:,j})\phi(\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z} - \mathbf{u}^T g_{\mathrm{c}}(\overline{\mathbf{L}})_{:,j} \mathbf{1}_n^T)$ where $\phi$ is a $\delta$-wide bump. Total $O(n(1/\delta)^{dn}/n!)$ layers.

nodes.name: Shift columns into disjoint cubes via positional encoding
nodes.statement: Choose $\mathbf{E}_{:,j} = (j-1)\mathbf{1}_d$, so $(\mathbf{X}+\mathbf{E})_{:,j} \in [j-1, j]^d$. Each column lies in its own disjoint cube.

nodes.name: Quantize over the union of column-specific grids
nodes.statement: Modify $g_{\mathrm{q}}$ to use $dn/\delta$ feed-forward layers covering $k = 0, \delta, \dots, n-\delta$, quantizing entries of $\mathbf{X}+\mathbf{E}$ into $[0:\delta:1-\delta]^d \times \dots \times [n-1:\delta:n-\delta]^d$.

nodes.name: Apply contextual mapping (Category 1 only)
nodes.statement: Stack $n(1/\delta)^d$ selective-shift attention layers and one global-shift layer; since $l_1 < \dots < l_n$ automatically, only Category 1 applies, so the analysis from $\mathrm{PSP16.12}$ carries over.

nodes.name: Value mapping without permutation symmetry
nodes.statement: Apply the value-mapping construction from Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.5}$ but using $O(n(1/\delta)^{dn})$ layers (no $1/n!$ saving since equivariance is dropped).

nodes.name: Half-shift $\psi(\mathbf{Z}; b_Q)$
nodes.statement: Compute $\psi(\mathbf{Z}; b_Q) = \mathbf{e}^{(1)} \mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z}\, \mathrm{hdmx}[(\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z})^T(\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z} - b_Q \mathbf{1}_n^T)]$, returning $\max_k \mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z}_{:,k}$ in the first row of column $j$ if $\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z}_{:,j} > b_Q$ and $\min_k$ otherwise.

nodes.name: Form difference $\Psi = \psi(\cdot; b_Q) - \psi(\cdot; b'_Q)$
nodes.statement: Combine two heads: $\Psi(\mathbf{Z}; b_Q, b'_Q) = \psi(\mathbf{Z}; b_Q) - \psi(\mathbf{Z}; b'_Q)$, which equals $\max - \min$ when $\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{Z}_{:,j} \in (b_Q, b'_Q)$ and $0$ outside.

nodes.name: Residual update of layer
nodes.statement: Output $\mathbf{Z} + \Psi(\mathbf{Z}; b_Q, b'_Q)$, which selectively shifts only those columns whose 'column id' lies in $(b_Q, b'_Q)$.

nodes.name: Apply $g_{\mathrm{q}}$ (feed-forward quantization)
nodes.statement: Use $\frac{d}{\delta}+d$ feed-forward layers to send $\mathbf{X}$ to $\mathbf{L} \in \mathbb{G}_\delta^+$ (Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.3}$).

nodes.name: Apply $g_{\mathrm{c}}$ (self-attention contextual mapping)
nodes.statement: Use $\delta^{-d}+1$ self-attention layers (each performing a selective shift) to compute the contextual mapping $g_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathbf{L})$ (Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.4}$).

nodes.name: Apply $g_{\mathrm{v}}$ (feed-forward value mapping)
nodes.statement: Use $O(n(1/\delta)^{dn}/n!)$ feed-forward layers to map each contextual embedding to the desired output column $(\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{L}})_{:,j}$ (Lemma $\mathrm{LP16.5}$).
